top_verse_en: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.

refs.t_en: He answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
And you are sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers, when He said to Abraham, 'Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.' . . .
Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent. . . .
I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit. . . .
For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the Jews on behalf of God's truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,
But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the Law,
He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.
He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him. . . .
But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, 'We do not want this man to rule over us.'
What shall I do?' asked the owner of the vineyard. 'I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.' . . .
You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did. . . .

outline.text_en: The divinity, humanity, office, and incarnation of Jesus Christ.
The calling of Simon and Andrew, Philip and Nathanael

parallel_en.text: He came to His own, and those who were His own did not receive Him.
He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
He came to His own, and His own people did not receive Him.
He came to his own creation, yet his own people did not receive him.
He came to what was his own, but his own people did not receive him.
He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
